verdict_text: NO. The script uses a naive greedy sequential packer with no special case forcing `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` into their own shard; since each is ~412 MB (under the 512 MiB/536,870,912-byte cap on its own), the greedy loop will keep appending subsequent layer tensors (input_layernorm, q/k/v/o_proj, etc.) to the same shard until the running total exceeds the cap, rather than isolating the large tensor alone. This violates the "Required result" §4 clause that `model.embed_tokens.weight` and `lm_head.weight` are each stored alone in their own shard, producing a shard layout that will not match the hidden reference's grouping even though total byte-per-shard limits are respected. The LoRA merge math itself (scale = alpha/r = 2, `B @ A` without transpose, prefix mapping, required assertions) is correct and matches the spec.
